steps.description: Pre-filter genes to those with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with suspected batch via SVA
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile shows 6 treated vs 6 control kidney samples with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) and no recorded processing batch, but the PCA reveals two clusters of six samples that do NOT align with condition — a hallmark of an unmodeled technical batch. Per the grounded procedure (Inflexa knowledge service, snapshot sha256:dfcde5f7e64089dd43007623dd938eeca4962364bac2e2ee6cb83880a7422101), the correct response is NOT to remove or adjust the counts by cluster membership (that would risk conflating batch with condition in an unbalanced way and inflate confidence), but to (1) confirm via QC that the PCA split truly does not track condition, library size, or gene detection artifacts; (2) since no processing variable is recorded to explain the split, estimate latent surrogate variables with sva using condition as the known factor of interest, and add them as covariates in the DESeq2 design; (3) run the Wald test on this extended design with apeglm shrinkage; (4) inspect the p-value histogram for residual batch inflation post-correction, falling back to fdrtool for an empirical null if irregular; (5) run fgsea preranked enrichment (Hallmark, then Reactome/WikiPathways/GO as available) on the Wald statistic; (6) report both the SVA-adjusted primary result and, since one PCA cluster could reflect a true outlier rather than a symmetric batch, a stated sensitivity check. All steps ground in the returned procedure; the design-covariate step is flagged (R-0025/R-0068) as the correct handling of a suspected-but-unrecorded batch, and R-0084 flags that a clean p-value histogram after SVA correction does not by itself prove the batch is resolved.

Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (smallest group size)
sva two-group surrogate variable estimation (condition as known factor), SVs added as covariates in design ~ SV1 + ... + condition
DESeq2 Wald test on design ~ SVs + condition
apeglm shrinkage of the condition coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg on Wald p-values with independent filtering, alpha=0.05; inspect p-value histogram, fdrtool empirical null fallback if irregular
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark human then Reactome human
DESeq2/fgsea report with diagnostics, sensitivity analysis (with/without cluster-suspected outlier), session info
